name: grok
$comment-quotaSignatures: observed 2026-09-25: a spent Grok Build balance ends the stream with {"type":"error","message":"Internal error: {\n  \"message\": \"API error (status 402 Payment Required): Grok Build usage balance exhausted\", ...}"}. Until this phrase was listed, that record read as a schema failure and the step was retried on grok itself. The generic phrasings (rate limit exceeded, too many requests, quota exceeded) come from DEFAULT_QUOTA_SIGNATURES in src/lib/quota.js.

eventStream.$comment-toolKinds: Tool names as grok 1.0.13 captured them in real streams (2026-09-19 and 2026-09-21 verify attempts): run_terminal_command, read_file, write, search_replace, grep, list_dir. todo_write, web_fetch and get_command_or_subagent_output were captured too and count as other.

rules.$comment-kind: An update carries no tool name, so it is captured as a tool result (`tool`, the kind claude-code's tool_result has) rather than the decoder's nameless `agent`; the Step page folds it into the tool_call with the same toolCallId.

eventStream.$comment-usage: verified 2026-09-21 against grok 1.0.13 and tests/fixtures/stream/grok-capture.jsonl, a real capture of the spawn argv (`grok -p <taskFile> --model grok-4.6 --session-id <uuid> --output-format streaming-json`, task 'Reply with the single word DONE.'): the final `end` line carries `sessionId`, `total_cost_usd` and `usage{input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, total_tokens}`, each the sum of the per-request `usage` lines (85680+1280 input/cache over two requests). input_tokens EXCLUDES cache reads (input 85680 + cacheRead 1280 + output 265 = total_tokens 87225) and output_tokens INCLUDES reasoning (reasoning is not added to total_tokens, and the request whose only visible text was `DONE` reported output 124 with reasoning 123). No model id rides the end line, only a `modelUsage` map keyed by the served model.

$comment-knownModels: Last-resort list for when `grok models` fails: what grok 1.0.40 listed on 2026-09-23 (grok-4.7 is its default). Successful discovery does not merge these entries.
$comment-reasoning: flag verified from `grok --help` (grok 1.0.13): `--reasoning-effort <EFFORT>  Reasoning effort for reasoning models  [aliases: --effort]`. Accepted values verified from the grok 1.0.13 binary's own validation message (`strings` on the executable): `invalid reasoning effort: (expected one of: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max)`. `none` and `minimal` sit below bullswarm's common scale, so a request below `low` clamps up to `low`. Tier defaults mirror claude-code (high=xhigh, medium=high, low=medium).
$comment-modelFamilies: Grok has one model line (owner decision, 2026-09-23). Every plain grok-N.M, with no suffix, is one family: high tier, rank 5, and the newest version wins, so a grok-4.8 takes over the day `grok models` lists it. grok-N.M-build-fast is Grok Build's id for the Fast variant, which https://docs.x.ai/developers/grok-4-7 (checked 2026-09-23) describes as 'the same model served on faster infrastructure, billed at twice the standard token rates'. It keeps its base model's rank and is never auto-recommended; it stays selectable by hand (strategy set-rung). Its family is named grok-build-fast so that, at equal rank, the plain grok family sorts first wherever models are ordered by rank alone.
$comment-generationFallback: Owner decision (2026-09-23), not a benchmark result: Grok has one model line, so medium and low run the newest grok-N.M too and differ from high only by reasoning. No family serves medium or low, so each tier takes the best-ranked family's newest model (grok-4.7 today) at the connector's own tier default (reasoning.defaults: high xhigh, medium high, low medium). The suggestion carries that level, so strategy apply writes it into the medium and low rungs the way it writes Codex's medium level.

medium.why: one Grok line, lighter reasoning for lighter tiers

low.why: one Grok line, lighter reasoning for lighter tiers

$comment-modelProfiles: Exact rows carry each model's dated price; tier and rank come from modelFamilies. Prices are per 1M tokens as https://docs.x.ai/docs/models listed them on 2026-09-23, the same numbers as https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing that day: grok-4.7 and grok-4.6 $2.00 input, $0.50 cached input, $6.00 output below 200k prompt tokens and $4.00, $1.00, $12.00 from 200k; grok-4.5 $2.00, $0.30, $6.00 and $4.00, $0.60, $12.00. grok-4.7-build-fast has no row on purpose. Doubling grok-4.7 gives $4.00, $1.00, $12.00 below 200k and $8.00, $2.00, $24.00 above, but the Pricing page's own Grok 4.7 Fast table (https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing#grok-47-fast-pricing-cursor-and-grok-build-only, 2026-09-23) lists $4.00, $1.00, $12.00 below 200k and $6.00, $1.50, $18.00 above. The long-context rates are not twice grok-4.7's, so a 2x row would be wrong there, and it stays unpriced until a row states which rate card it follows.
$comment-timeout: No implicit wall-clock timeout; callers may opt in with --timeout or workflow step.timeoutSec
$comment-meter: weekly shared credit pool via billing endpoint; no 5h window exists on unified-billing accounts
